messages.author: 0505f504492a4cae
messages.subject: Issue with warping surfaces: plotRefToTarget
parts:
Hello,

I have run into an issue warping 3D meshes to targets (in this case to PC extremes) using the plotRefToTarget function. I can get the surface to warp, but the warp does not match the PC extreme I have designated. Effectively, the surface file is smooshed anterolaterally which is not accurate to the variation captured in the PC. I have been able to plot a wireframe of the PC extremes using the plotRefToTarget function successfully, but I am unable to warp the surface. 

I think the error is coming in at the creation of the average mesh, specifically at  'mean.coords' (below) as I am using the procrustes transformed coordinates which technically would not align with the .ply file. However, when I try to load in my coordinates from the .landmarkASCII file (i.e. #mean.coords2) I get the following error: "Error in warpRefMesh(mean.ply, mean.coords2, avg, color = NULL, centered = FALSE) :  Input must be a p-x-k matrix of landmark coordinates". I'm not sure how to correct this issue. 

Does anyone have any advice on resolving this?

I have provided a my code here: 

lmcoords <- coords.all[["coords"]]    # coordinates created from multiple files for the same species using 'combine.subsets'
Y.gpa <- gpagen(lmcoords, Proj = TRUE, PrinAxes = TRUE)
ref <-mshape(Y.gpa$coords)
   
var <- Y.gpa[["coords"]]
avg <-mshape(var)    
findMeanSpec(var)    # species closest to mean = 38, Tamiasciurus
   
mean.ply <- read.ply("Tamiasciurus-hudsonicus.ply", ShowSpecimen=FALSE)
mean.coords <- Y.gpa$coords[,,38] # 38 is the sequence number for the mean species
#mean.coords2 <- read.amira.set("Tamiasciurus_hudsonicus.landmarkAscii",36) 
       
averagemesh <- warpRefMesh(mean.ply, mean.coords, avg, color=NULL, centered=FALSE) 
   
PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)
PC1min <- PCA$shapes$shapes.comp1$min
   
plotRefToTarget(M1 = mean.coords, M2 = PC1min, mesh = averagemesh, color = gray, method = "surface")

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: Issue with warping surfaces: plotRefToTarget
parts:
Without data, my guess is: You are using the mean shape coordinates to create the averamesh object, but actually giving the PLY file that has the real specimen in it. Because the mean.coords is after the procrustest superimposition, it is unlikely that those coordinates would be on the 3D model of your specimen

Normally this is a two-step process: You deformed the closest sample (using its own coordinate data) to the mean shape and create mean model, and then you use the mean model to visualize the PCs.

messages.author: e358c6bea2b9961c
messages.subject: Re: Issue with warping surfaces: plotRefToTarget
parts:
Hi Maddy,

I encountred the same problem in the past and I found some code to solve this likely on this forum. Anyway here it is:

#Find specimen closer to mean, useful to create warp mesh
findMeanSpec(coords) #number below specimen name is the number of the specimen in the array

#Create object containing only that specimen coordinates
warp_specimen <- coords[,,23] #number displayed by findMeanSpec
warp_specimen

#Import simplified mesh to create warp mesh on
mesh_3D <- vcgImport("Data/refmesh.ply") #make sure NO binary encoding (ASCII)

#Check range of mesh and coordinates to make sure it has same scale
range(mesh_3D$vb[1:3,]) #if this is too big/small, scale in editor and re-import
range(warp_specimen)

##Create warp mesh, to use as reference for visualization of analyses
ref_mesh <- warpRefMesh(mesh = mesh_3D, mesh.coord = warp_specimen, ref = mean_shape, color = "gray", centered = FALSE)

Then ref_mesh is what you need to apply plotRefToTarget to to get your PC extremes. 
To scale the mesh I use the free software Meshlab. I usally need to reduce the mesh to about 100th of its original size (if it was 20 cm in lenght, it will become 0.02 cm), but that will depend on your samples. Just look at the differences in decimals you get from the range function. If the mesh shows values like 20 - 30 and your warp speciemen coordinates are 0.02 - 0.03 you would need to reduce the mesh by 100 and so forth.
Depending on how great the deformation is and your specific samples, the plotRefToTarget mesh might be better or worse than just using points for example, but if it works well it's a very nice visualization. 

Hope this helps!
Best wishes,
Agnese

messages.author: 0505f504492a4cae
messages.subject: Re: Issue with warping surfaces: plotRefToTarget
parts:
Hello, 

Thank you both for your replies! I was able to properly warp the mesh.

The issue was in the coordinates I was using to create the average mesh (as Murat pointed out). In my original code I was calling the gpa transformed coordinates of the mean species which did not fit the scale of .ply file. I had suspected this was the issue, but I was having trouble loading in the untransformed coordinates without an error message. I am also combining several landmark sets per species (1 traditional landmark file and 2 sliding landmark files) using the 'combine.subsets' function to create my 'coords.all' assignment. As I learned through troubleshooting this, while you can specify the combine.subsets function not to perform a GPA it will still adjust all centroid sizes to 1.0 (unless otherwise specified) which would have also made it inappropriate to use to create the average mesh. Knowing this, I decided to combine all three landmarks files for each species by hand and was able to call the untransformed coords for the mean species to create the average mesh. 

I'm not sure if it's helpful, but I am including the code I used to do this with annotation:

## WARPING SURFACES ##
    GDF <- geomorph.data.frame(landmarks = coords.all)    # could probably use your matrix of lm coords, but as I was having issues getting my coords from my matrix (coords.all) so I created a geomorph dataframe with raw coords
   
    Y.gpa <- gpagen(coords.all, curves = sliders)    # run gpa with curves designated (for my data the slider were defined using 'define.sliders' function)
    ref <-mshape(Y.gpa$coords)                               # get coords for the mean shape from the transformed landmark matrix
       
    var <- Y.gpa[["coords"]]
    avg <-mshape(var)     # calculate the mean shape
    findMeanSpec(var)    # identify species closest to mean
   
    mean.ply <- read.ply("Tamiasciurus-hudsonicus.ply", ShowSpecimen=FALSE)    # load the .ply for the mean species
    mean.coords <- coords.all[,,38]            # get the untransformed coordinates for the mean specimen/species (38 is the sequence number for the mean species (i.e. Tamiasciurus hudsonicus))
    ygpa.mc <- Y.gpa$coords[,,38]             # get transformed coords (from Y.gpa) for the mean specimen/species
       
    averagemesh <- warpRefMesh(mean.ply, mean.coords, avg, color=NULL, centered=FALSE)   # create a mesh of the average shape
   
    PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)                       # need to run a PCA to get the extremes for PCs
    PC1min <- PCA$shapes$shapes.comp1$min    # identify the coords for the min of PC1 (comp1)
   
    plotRefToTarget(M1 = ygpa.mc, M2 = PC1min, mesh = averagemesh, method = "surface")    # warp averagemesh to the coords at PC1min

Best, 
Maddy
